name: Type IIa fibre (fast oxidative-glycolytic)
short_description: The middle fibre of the three human skeletal muscle types: fast like Type IIx, but with enough mitochondria and myoglobin to also run oxidatively, giving it noticeably better fatigue resistance than its purely glycolytic sibling. A single, unbranched, cylindrical multinucleated cell centimetres long (~30 mm) and ~60 µm across — narrower than Type IIx, wider than Type I — cross-striated by regular transverse A/I banding along its whole length, with many flattened nuclei just under the sarcolemma at the periphery (never one central nucleus — that is cardiac muscle), a moderate density of mitochondria and a moderate surrounding capillary network (more than Type IIx, less than Type I), and a pale rose-pink colour that sits visibly between Type I's deep red and Type IIx's near-white cream. Endurance training shifts some Type IIx fibres toward IIa; disuse pushes the balance back.

textbook.4: pass (gemini-3-pro-image, same prompt as attempt 3 re-rolled on the pro tier). Zoomed crops of the outer fibre body (top-left corner, bottom-right corner, and the general surface outside the cutaway) all show continuous transverse A/I banding with fine slate Z-lines running the full visible length, WITH fine lengthwise myofibril striping underneath — both patterns present at once, and this time the transverse banding covers the outer body correctly, not just the cutaway window. Framing verified at both opposite extreme corners: fibre body colour fills each corner edge-to-edge, no background triangle, no end-cap. >=7 peripheral nuclei counted, all on the rim, none central. Mitochondria moderate — visibly more numerous/clustered than a sparse scatter but not a dense packed carpet, correctly between Type I and Type IIx. Glycogen granules present, modest. Capillary a single smooth continuous crimson line, no candy-cane artefact. Colour a pale rose-pink, correctly between Type I's deep red and Type IIx's near-white cream. No baked text. No border on any of the 4 edges. Used as final; 10-label SVG built against this base image, every anchor pixel-sampled against the raw (unlabelled) render, not just the rasterised SVG composite (whose leader-line strokes cover the exact anchor pixel and would otherwise read as the line colour, not the structure — confirmed empirically: sampling exactly at (ax,ay) on the cairosvg-rasterised composite returns the leader-line/halo colour almost every time; the fix used is sampling a small offset perpendicular to the leader line, plus a direct check against the un-annotated base PNG at the exact anchor coordinate).

sem.3: pass (gemini-3-pro-image, prompt rewritten with a closed-loop 'earthworm segment / bellows accordion / corrugated drainage pipe' analogy stating explicitly that each ridge is a CLOSED RING that returns to its own starting point without ever moving toward either end of the tube — this framing, not just tier escalation, is what fixed it). Zoomed crops (centre, extreme top-left corner, extreme bottom-right corner) all show genuine closed transverse rings wrapping the tube's full circumference, evenly spaced the entire visible length, with no lengthwise ridge anywhere. Framing verified at both extreme corners: fibre body fills each corner edge-to-edge, no background triangle, no end-cap. Long shallow oval bulges along both flanks consistent with peripheral nuclei pushing against the sarcolemma from inside (the only honest way a surface-only SEM can gesture at nuclear position). Pale rose-pink false colour, correctly between Type I (deep red) and Type IIx (near-white cream). No baked text, no border, single dominant specimen. Used as final. Surface-only medium — per project convention, no labelled SVG built for SEM (interior structures like bands/Z-disc/mitochondria/glycogen are not visible in a genuine SEM). Revised prompt recorded in prompts.json in place of the original, with a note on why.

reference: pass (2026-08-21, verified by a previous agent in this same session before the render/annotation work began). PLOS ONE Figure 1A (Bloemberg & Quadrilatero 2012), multicolor immunofluorescence transverse cross-section of rat tibialis anterior, CC BY 4.0. Distinct green-stained fibre profiles are unambiguously labelled IIA in the original figure among blue I / red IIB / black IIX / dark-green IIAX fibres — a genuine protocol-identified positive for Type IIa, the one thing a single-pH ATPase plate (used/rejected by the sibling subjects) cannot provide. Honest caveats already on record in §2: rat tissue not human (same antibody protocol validated on human muscle in the source paper); baked-in text labels kept deliberately since they are the point of choosing this plate, never used as an SVG base; a transverse cross-section, so it cannot show cross-striation/nuclear position/length (those are verified against the AI renders instead); thin ~4px composite-figure border left as-is (documentary photograph, not a generated image).

used as final (gemini-2.5-flash-image, attempt 2). Playful jogging fibre character, sweatband, motion-swoosh lines, two bean-shaped mitochondria friends, a thin capillary line, cross-stripe hints; no starburst anywhere and no border on any of the 4 edges (confirmed by scanning all four edge rows/columns for dark pixels: zero found on all four). COMPROMISE, stated plainly rather than smoothed over: the brief called for the artwork to bleed off all four edges, and it does not — the character sits centered with a generous white margin on all sides, in both attempt 1 and a second attempt with substantially stronger 'zoom in, crop the body at two edges' framing language. This is the same behaviour already present (and previously accepted) in this set's type-i-fibre and type-iix-fibre coloring pages, whose own verdicts logged 'runs off all 4 edges' despite the archived PNGs showing the same centered, margined composition — flagged here rather than repeating that unverified claim. No border/starburst (the two genuinely unrecoverable failures) makes this usable; the non-bleed is a real but lower-severity miss, recorded in PLAN.md rather than burned through more attempts against an apparent flash-tier tendency to center the subject regardless of framing wording.
